title: Cost bounds for the learning program
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $t>0$ and $0<\varepsilon\le\tfrac12$ be rational, and let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function. Every outcome in the support of the program's cost distribution on target $f$ uses at most the monotone bounded-influence random-example budget, makes exactly zero membership queries, and incurs work at most the monotone bounded-influence work budget, with parameters $n,t,\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
The outcome belongs to the support of the program's cost distribution for target $f$
